subject: Renewal + EU residency / APAC rollout timing and failover
messages:
From: Anna Schmidt <anna.schmidt@medicorp.eu>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@medicorp.eu>
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2028 09:12:00 +0200
Subject: Renewal kickoff — residency and APAC questions

Hi Jordan,

Hope you’re well. Our renewal is coming up (contract expires 2028-08-01) and the executive team wants clarity on three items before we move to E&C:

1) EU data residency — we need an explicit commitment that production workloads and token logs for our EU tenancy will stay in the Frankfurt region by default.
2) APAC onramp — we’re planning a phased APAC rollout in Q4 and need an estimate for how fast we can bring a dedicated APAC pool online and what uplift that introduces to pricing.
3) Cross-region failover — we require a failover map and SLA (what does failover mean for data residency guarantees?).

I’ve attached a short procurement questionnaire with our standard legal/security asks. Can you loop in whoever handles residency commitments and a solutions engineer to confirm timelines?

Thanks,
Anna
Anna Schmidt
Head of Cloud Procurement, Medicorp Health
anna.schmidt@medicorp.eu
+49 30 1234 5678

Attachment: procurement-questionnaire.xlsx (xlsx, 42 KB)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Anna Schmidt <anna.schmidt@medicorp.eu>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2028 11:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Renewal kickoff — residency and APAC questions

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (your AE) and Vivek (solutions) to scope the commitments and translate to contract language.

Quick answers at a high level:
- EU residency: we can guarantee that production inference and token logs for your EU tenant remain in the Frankfurt (eu-central-1) tenancy. We propose adding an appendix to the SOW that maps tenant IDs to region and specifies the log retention & location.
- APAC onramp: our typical lead time for a dedicated APAC pool (reserved GPUs + dedicated routing) is 8–10 weeks from kickoff. For a faster path we offer a burst-enabled approach (shared capacity with soft isolation) that can be live in ~3 weeks but with a predictable uplift.
- Failover: our standard cross-region failover is active-passive with cold KVS replication and warm caches in the failover region. Failover preserves model artifacts but the token residency guarantee applies only when traffic is served from the pinned region; during failover we document the exception and the acceptable audit trail.

I’ve attached the draft SOW (v3) with proposed appendix language and an initial pricing uplift for APAC burst. Marissa — can you confirm the commercial uplift and whether Medicorp is eligible for a multi-year pricing guarantee? Vivek — can you confirm the technical playbook (runbook link below) so we can feed that into the SOW?

Next: we’ll review the procurement questionnaire and produce redlines and a proposed amendment for residency/failover.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

Attachment: Medicorp_RI_SOW_v3.pdf (pdf, 210 KB)
Links: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ExampleRunbook

From: Anna Schmidt <anna.schmidt@medicorp.eu>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@medicorp.eu>
Date: Sat, 15 Jun 2028 08:35:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Renewal kickoff — residency and APAC questions

Jordan — thanks, that helps. A few clarifications from procurement/legal: 

• Residency appendix: we will need (a) tenant ID mapping, (b) an explicit sentence that logs at rest remain within eu-central-1 for the duration of the agreement except in documented failover events, and (c) certification of physical region where backups are stored.

• Failover SLA: our security team is asking for an RTO/RPO expectation and clarity that during failover a formal incident record is created and shared. Can you confirm the RTO target and whether failover triggers an exception to EU-only residency (we understand there may be short-term routing implications but need the audit language).

• APAC pricing: we prefer the dedicated pool option if the lead time can be shortened to 6 weeks with an onboarding plan; otherwise we’ll accept burst for initial Q4 traffic. Please send a priced amendment that shows (i) dedicated pool cost, (ii) burst cost, and (iii) uplift for geo-replication of KV caches.

Also — please send SOC 2 evidence and any recent penetration test summary to speed our GRC review. I’ve attached the procurement questionnaire we began to fill.

Regards,
Anna

Attachment: procurement-questionnaire.xlsx (xlsx, 90 KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Anna Schmidt <anna.schmidt@medicorp.eu>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Jun 2028 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal kickoff — residency and APAC questions

Hi Anna — thanks for the detailed list and for starting the questionnaire. I’ll keep this practical and list what we can commit to in the renewal amendment: 

1) Residency appendix & backups: we will:
   - Map tenant ID Medicorp-EU-01 in the appendix to eu-central-1 by name and AZ set.
   - Add language: "All production inference and token logs for tenant Medicorp-EU-01 will be stored at rest in eu-central-1. Short-term exceptions during documented failover events are allowed as defined in Section X."
   - Provide a separate exhibit stating where backups are stored (primary backup in eu-central-1, secondary encrypted snapshots in eu-west-1 for DR).

2) Failover SLA and runbook: proposed RTO = 2 hours for regional failover; RPO = 15 minutes for KV replication on the tiered plan (15m for dedicated, 60m for burst). We will produce an incident record template and commit to sharing post-incident timelines and logs. Vivek — I’ve asked you to attach the runbook excerpt and the incident template; leaving that to you.

3) APAC onramp pricing options:
   - Dedicated APAC pool: target lead time 6–8 weeks with a 12% uplift on base dedicated pricing for initial capacity; includes geo-replication of metrics and per-tenant routing.
   - Burst-enabled APAC (fast path): live in ~3 weeks, 7% uplift, soft isolation (no dedicated GPU reservation).

Commercial ask: if Medicorp signs a 24-month renewal with a committed APAC capacity baseline we can hold dedicated pricing to a 10% uplift instead of 12% and provide a 90-day SLA credit for first-year onboarding issues.

Security evidence: attaching latest SOC 2 summary + summary of last external pentest (redacted). We’ll deliver more detailed artifacts under NDA if you need them.

Next steps I propose:
- Jordan/Marissa to deliver SOW v3 redlines with the residency appendix and two priced APAC options by Tue 2028-06-19.
- Medicorp to return signed procurement questionnaire and confirm preferred APAC path.
- We’ll prepare a DocuSign amendment (link below) after redlines.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0133

Attachments: SOC2-evidence-summary.pdf (pdf, 120 KB); Medicorp_RI_SOW_v3.pdf (updated with notes)
Links: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/8421, https://www.docusign.com/EN/sign/abcdef
